q: According to the first account of creation, God created the firmament on the _____ day.
explanation: In Genesis 1:6-8, God created the firmament (the expanse) on the second day to separate the waters from the waters.

q: The creation of man in the second account of creation was primarily from _____.
explanation: Genesis 2:7 states that the Lord God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.

q: Joseph was sold by his brothers to the Ishmaelites for _____ pieces of silver.
explanation: According to Genesis 37:28, Joseph's brothers sold him to the Midianite/Ishmaelite traders for twenty shekels of silver.

q: God's promise to Abraham that he would be the father of many nations was sealed with the sign of _____.
explanation: In Genesis 17, God established circumcision as the physical sign of the covenant between Him and Abraham's descendants.

q: Moses' father-in-law, who advised him on how to delegate judicial duties, was _____.
explanation: Jethro, the priest of Midian, observed Moses wearing himself out and advised him to appoint capable men as leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

q: The passover feast was instituted in Egypt to commemorate the _____.
opts: sparing of the first-born of the Israelites
explanation: The Passover was established so the Angel of Death would pass over the houses marked with lamb's blood, sparing the Israelite first-borns.

q: The golden calf made by the Israelites in the wilderness was facilitated by _____.
explanation: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, the people pressured Aaron, who took their gold and fashioned it into a molten calf.

q: Which of the following women was a judge in Israel?
explanation: Deborah was a prophetess and the only female judge mentioned in the Book of Judges who led Israel to victory over Jabin's army.

q: The high priest who fell and died upon hearing that the Ark of God had been captured was _____.
explanation: Eli died at age ninety-eight when he heard the news of the capture of the Ark and the death of his two sons.

q: Saul was rejected as king over Israel primarily because of his _____.
opts: disobedience to God's command regarding the Amalekites
explanation: 1 Samuel 15 records that Saul spared Agag and the best of the livestock, violating God's command of total destruction (herem).

q: David's sin with Bathsheba was exposed by the prophet _____.
explanation: Prophet Nathan used a parable about a rich man stealing a poor man's ewe lamb to convict David of his adultery and murder.

q: The wisdom of Solomon was notably demonstrated in his judgment between _____.
opts: two harlots claiming a living child
explanation: Solomon proposed to divide the living child in half, knowing the real mother would prefer to give up the child than see it killed.

q: The division of the kingdom of Israel took place during the reign of _____.
explanation: Rehoboam's refusal to lighten the labor yoke imposed by his father Solomon led to the rebellion of the ten northern tribes.

q: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal took place on Mount _____.
explanation: Mount Carmel was the site where Elijah proved that Yahweh is God by calling down fire to consume the sacrifice.

q: The prophet who was a shepherd from Tekoa and preached against social injustice was _____.
explanation: Amos was a simple shepherd and dresser of sycamore trees who fearlessly condemned the wealthy for oppressing the poor.

q: Hosea’s marriage to _____ was a symbolic representation of God’s relationship with unfaithful Israel.
explanation: God commanded Hosea to marry an unfaithful woman (Gomer) to illustrate Israel's spiritual adultery through idol worship.

q: The king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and took the people into exile was _____.
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar II led the siege that resulted in the burning of the Temple and the deportation of the Jews to Babylon.

q: Nehemiah's primary mission in Jerusalem was to _____.
opts: rebuild the walls of the city
explanation: Nehemiah was the cupbearer to the Persian king who obtained permission to return to Jerusalem to rebuild its broken walls.

q: According to the Gospel of Luke, the angel who announced the birth of Jesus to Mary was _____.
explanation: Luke 1:26 states that the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city in Galilee named Nazareth.

q: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the census ordered by _____.
explanation: Luke 2 records that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be registered.

q: John the Baptist's message centered on 'Repent, for the _____ is at hand'.
explanation: Matthew 3:2 records John preaching in the wilderness of Judea, announcing the proximity of the Kingdom of Heaven.

q: Jesus was baptized by John in the River Jordan to _____.
opts: show He was a disciple of John
explanation: In Matthew 3:15, Jesus told John to permit the baptism to 'fulfill all righteousness', identifying with humanity.

q: During the temptation, the devil asked Jesus to turn stones into bread to test His _____.
explanation: The temptation 'If you are the Son of God...' was an attempt to make Jesus use His divine power for selfish physical needs.

q: The first four disciples called by Jesus were _____.
explanation: Mark 1:16-20 records the calling of the two pairs of brothers: Simon (Peter) and Andrew, then James and John.

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught that the _____ shall inherit the earth.
explanation: Matthew 5:5 (The Beatitudes) states: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth'.

q: The miracle of the feeding of the five thousand involved _____.
opts: seven loaves and a few fish
explanation: Matthew 14:17 specifies the boy's offering was five barley loaves and two fish.

q: The Transfiguration of Jesus took place in the presence of _____.
explanation: Jesus took the inner circle of Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain where He was transfigured before them.

q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, the two religious figures who passed by the wounded man were a _____ and a _____.
explanation: Luke 10:31-32 mentions that first a priest and then a Levite saw the man and passed by on the other side.

q: The parable of the Prodigal Son was primarily told to illustrate _____.
opts: the love and forgiveness of God
explanation: The father's reception of the lost son represents God's joy and eagerness to welcome back repentant sinners.

q: The request of the sons of Zebedee for positions of honor in Jesus’ kingdom showed their _____.
explanation: James and John sought seats at the right and left of Jesus, failing to understand that greatness in His kingdom comes through service and suffering.

q: Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem on a donkey was a fulfillment of the prophecy of _____.
explanation: Zechariah 9:9 prophesied the King coming to Zion 'humble and riding on a donkey'.

q: At the Last Supper, the bread represents Jesus’ _____.
explanation: Jesus took bread, blessed it, and said, 'Take, eat; this is my body' (Matthew 26:26).

q: The garden where Jesus prayed in agony before His arrest was _____.
explanation: Gethsemane, located on the Mount of Olives, was the site where Jesus asked that 'this cup' might pass from Him.

q: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus with a _____.
explanation: Judas used a kiss as the signal to the soldiers to identify which man was Jesus.

q: The Jewish high priest who presided over the trial of Jesus was _____.
explanation: Caiaphas was the high priest that year who organized the plot to kill Jesus.

q: The Roman Governor who reluctantly sentenced Jesus to death was _____.
explanation: Pilate found no guilt in Jesus but gave in to the pressure of the crowd to avoid a riot.

q: The criminal who was released instead of Jesus was _____.
explanation: The crowd chose Barabbas, a notorious prisoner/insurrectionist, to be released according to the custom of the feast.

q: Jesus was crucified at a place called Golgotha, which means _____.
explanation: Golgotha is an Aramaic word meaning 'Skull', referring to the hill's shape or its function as an execution site.

q: The person who provided the tomb for the burial of Jesus was _____.
explanation: Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy member of the Council, asked Pilate for the body and placed it in his own new tomb.

q: The resurrection of Jesus took place on the _____ day.
explanation: Biblical accounts and creeds affirm that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day (Friday to Sunday morning).

q: Before His ascension, Jesus commanded His disciples to wait in Jerusalem for the _____.
explanation: Acts 1:4-5 records Jesus telling them to wait for the Holy Spirit who would empower them.

q: The replacement for Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles was _____.
explanation: In Acts 1, the disciples cast lots and the lot fell on Matthias to join the eleven apostles.

q: The Holy Spirit descended on the disciples on the Day of _____.
explanation: Pentecost, a Jewish harvest festival occurring 50 days after Passover, was when the disciples spoke in tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.

q: The first Christian martyr was _____.
explanation: Stephen, one of the first seven deacons, was stoned to death for his testimony about Jesus (Acts 7).

q: Saul's conversion took place on the road to _____.
explanation: Saul was traveling to Damascus to arrest Christians when he was blinded by a light and heard the voice of Jesus.

q: The first place where the disciples were called 'Christians' was _____.
explanation: Acts 11:26 notes that it was in Antioch (Syria) that the name 'Christian' was first applied to believers.

q: The Jerusalem Council (Acts 15) met primarily to discuss _____.
explanation: The council determined that Gentile believers did not need to be circumcised or follow the whole Mosaic Law to be saved.

q: Paul was known as the 'Apostle to the _____'.
explanation: Paul received a specific commission to preach the Gospel to the non-Jewish world (Gentiles).

q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 13, the greatest virtue is _____.
explanation: Paul concludes the chapter by stating: 'So now faith, hope, and love abide... but the greatest of these is love'.

q: James teaches that 'faith by itself, if it has no _____, is dead'.
explanation: James 2:17 emphasizes that true saving faith will naturally result in good deeds or 'works'.

q: The person who helped Jesus carry the cross was _____.
explanation: As Jesus was led away, the soldiers seized Simon of Cyrene and laid the cross on him to carry it behind Jesus.

q: God's promise to Noah was symbolized by a _____.
explanation: Genesis 9:13 describes the rainbow as the sign of the covenant that God would never again destroy all life with a flood.

q: The son of Abraham born to the Egyptian maid Hagar was _____.
explanation: Ishmael was Abraham's first son, born when Sarah remained childless.

q: The first king of Israel was _____.
explanation: Saul was anointed by Samuel after the people of Israel demanded a king to be like other nations.

q: The city of Jericho was captured by the Israelites under the leadership of _____.
explanation: Joshua led the miraculous fall of Jericho's walls after circling the city for seven days.

q: Samson's strength was tied to his vow as a _____.
explanation: As a Nazirite, Samson was consecrated to God from birth, and one of his conditions was never to cut his hair.

q: The mother of Samuel was _____.
explanation: Hannah was barren but prayed fervently at the temple in Shiloh, and God gave her Samuel.

q: Solomon built the Temple of the Lord in the city of _____.
explanation: Jerusalem was the capital and the religious center where the First Temple was constructed.

q: The prophet who challenged King Ahab and Queen Jezebel was _____.
explanation: Elijah was the fierce opponent of the cult of Baal introduced by Jezebel in the Northern Kingdom.

q: The 'Valley of Dry Bones' vision was seen by Prophet _____.
explanation: Ezekiel 37 records this vision symbolizing the restoration and spiritual revival of the house of Israel.

q: Jesus healed a man born blind by using _____.
explanation: John 9:6 records Jesus spitting on the ground, making mud with the saliva, and anointing the man's eyes.

q: The disciple who doubted the resurrection until he saw Jesus' wounds was _____.
explanation: Thomas, also called Didymus, said he would not believe unless he could touch the nail marks in Jesus' hands.

q: The gift of the Magi that symbolized Jesus’ future death and burial was _____.
explanation: Myrrh was an expensive resin used for embalming bodies, prefiguring Christ's sacrifice.

q: Paul wrote the Letter to the Romans primarily to explain _____.
explanation: Romans is Paul’s most systematic theological work, focusing on how humans are made right with God through faith in Christ.

q: The Roman Centurion who sought Jesus to heal his servant showed great _____.
explanation: Jesus marveled at the Centurion's faith, saying He had not found such great faith even in Israel.

q: Ananias and Sapphira died because they _____.
opts: lied to the Holy Spirit about the proceeds of a sale
explanation: They kept back part of the money from a land sale while pretending to give the full amount to the church (Acts 5).

q: The specific sin of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah according to Genesis was _____.
explanation: The cities were destroyed because their outcry reached heaven and their sin was very grave.

q: The 'Great Commission' involves _____.
explanation: Matthew 28:19 records Jesus' final command to go, baptize, and teach all nations.

q: In the parable of the Sower, the 'seed' represents _____.
explanation: Jesus explained that the seed is the Word of God being sown into different types of human hearts.

q: According to Christian teaching, the 'wages of sin is death', but the 'free gift of God is _____' in Christ Jesus.
explanation: Romans 6:23 contrasts the consequence of sin with the gracious gift of eternal life through Christ.
